exposure: Home visits by community health workers
Attendance at family conversations during pregnancy
Mode of delivery (cesarean section or vaginal)
cohort: Women who had live births in the 12 months preceding the survey in Amhara, Oromia, SNNP, and Tigray regions of Ethiopia
finding: Community-level interactions and promotive health services, including antepartum home visits by community health workers, family conversation, birth notification, and being recognized as a model family, were significant determinants of postnatal care utilization.
mod_finding: Cesarean section mode of delivery was significantly associated with increased uptake of postnatal care.
